target_units.text: and the sin which he has committed becomes known unto him, he shall bring as his gift an unblemished male young goat from the goats.
And he shall lay his hand upon the young goat’s head; and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the whole burnt offerings before the Lord. It is a sin offering.

And the priest shall put some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger upon the horns of the altar of whole burnt offerings; and he shall pour out all its blood beside the base of the altar of whole burnt offerings.
And he shall offer up all its fat upon the altar, as the fat of a sacrifice of deliverance. And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin, and he shall be forgiven.

triples.relationship: related cattle and unblemished rams in consecratory instructions
triples.rationale: After the atonement, Ezekiel's instructions call for an unblemished calf and ram. Exodus's priestly consecration instructions likewise name a calf and unblemished rams, there two rams. The shared animal types and consecratory setting do not erase the stated numbers.
triples.source_text: After you have completed the atonement, they will bring an unblemished calf from the cattle and an unblemished ram from the sheep.

target_units.text: “This is what you shall do for them: consecrate them to serve Me as priests. Take one calf from the herd and two rams without blemish,

triples.relationship: close requirement to add salt to offerings
triples.rationale: Ezekiel's priests throw salt upon the animals before offering them as burnt offerings. Leviticus commands salt with every sacrificial gift and names the salt of the covenant. The salt requirement is shared; the target's covenant expression is not supplied as a quotation from Ezekiel.
triples.source_text: You all will bring them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt upon them and offer them as burnt offerings to the Lord.

target_units.text: And every gift of your sacrifice shall be seasoned with salt. You shall not let the salt of the covenant of the Lord cease from your sacrifices; with every gift of yours you shall bring salt unto the Lord your God.

triples.relationship: close seven-day consecratory offering prescriptions
triples.rationale: Ezekiel specifies seven days of offerings, including a kid for sin each day and unblemished cattle and a ram. Exodus likewise orders seven days for consecration and altar purification and names the calf for sin. The seven-day framework connects them while the different animal lists remain distinct.
triples.source_text: For seven days you will prepare a kid for sin each day, and a calf from the cattle and a ram from the sheep. They will prepare unblemished animals—

target_units.text: Do this for Aaron and his sons according to everything I commanded you. Consecrate their hands for seven days.
And you shall offer the calf for sin on the day of purification, and purify the altar when you perform consecration upon it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy; everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified.

triples.relationship: close seven-day altar purification and consecration of hands
triples.rationale: The source requires seven days of atoning for and cleansing the altar and filling the priests' hands. Exodus likewise joins seven days of consecrating hands with seven days of purifying and consecrating the altar. The parallel concerns these joined consecratory actions rather than a merely repeated number.
triples.source_text: —for seven days. They will make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they will fill their hands.

target_units.text: Do this for Aaron and his sons according to everything I commanded you. Consecrate their hands for seven days.
And you shall offer the calf for sin on the day of purification, and purify the altar when you perform consecration upon it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy; everyone who touches the altar shall be sanctified.

triples.relationship: close eighth-day sacrificial service after consecration
triples.rationale: From the eighth day the priests offer burnt and well-being offerings and God promises acceptance. Leviticus begins the eighth day's service with burnt offerings and a sacrifice of deliverance and promises the Lord's appearance. The common day and commencement of service connect them, with acceptance and appearance preserved as different statements.
triples.source_text: From the eighth day onward, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your offerings for well-being on the altar. I will accept you, says the Lord.”

target_units.text: And it came to pass on the eighth day that Moses called Aaron and his sons and the council of elders of Israel.
And Moses said unto Aaron: Take unto yourself a calf from the cattle for sin, and a ram for a whole burnt offering, unblemished, and present them before the Lord.
And speak unto the council of elders of Israel, saying: Take one male young goat from the goats for sin, and a calf and a year-old lamb, unblemished, for a whole offering,
and a calf and a ram for a sacrifice of deliverance before the Lord, and fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you.

triples.relationship: related closures of distinct east-facing gates
triples.rationale: This source describes the outer sanctuary gate facing east as shut. The later instruction concerns the inner-court east gate, shut on six working days but opened on Sabbaths and new moons. The locations and closure provisions are distinguished rather than treated as a contradiction about one gate.
triples.source_text: He brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the holy places, which faced east, and it was shut.

target_units.text: “Thus says the Lord God: The gate in the inner court facing east will be shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened, and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.

triples.relationship: close divine passage through the east-facing gate
triples.rationale: The gate will remain shut because the Lord God of Israel will enter through it. The earlier vision describes the Lord's glory entering the house through the east-facing gate. The common route is explicit, while the source's future entry is not silently changed into the target's past action.
triples.source_text: The Lord said to me, “This gate will remain shut. It will not be opened, and no one will pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, will enter through it. It will remain shut,

target_units.text: The glory of the Lord entered the house by the way of the gate facing east.

triples.relationship: close correspondence of the ruler's gate entry and departure
triples.rationale: The ruler enters by the gate's porch and goes out by his way, with eating bread before the Lord as the stated purpose here. The later instruction again makes the ruler enter by the porch and go out by the gate. The later unit does not separately repeat the meal.
triples.source_text: for the ruler—he will sit in it to eat bread before the Lord. He will enter by the way of the gate’s porch and go out by his way.”

target_units.text: When the ruler enters, he will enter by the porch of the gate and go out by the way of the gate.

triples.relationship: close glory filling the house and a human response before it
triples.rationale: Ezekiel sees the Lord's house full of glory and falls on his face. At Solomon's dedication the Lord's glory fills the house and the priests cannot stand to minister. The sanctuary-filling presence is shared, while the particular human responses differ.
triples.source_text: He brought me by the north gate opposite the house. I looked, and behold—the house of the Lord was full of glory. I fall on my face.

target_units.text: When the priests came out of the Holy Place, the cloud filled the house.
The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the Lord’s glory filled the house.

triples.relationship: close repeated demand for attentive eyes, ears and heart
triples.rationale: God now commands Ezekiel to set his heart, see and hear the house's ordinances and entrances. The earlier guide gave the same threefold demand before showing the vision for Israel. The repetition marks attentive reception of the house's instruction without equating the two speakers.
triples.source_text: The Lord said to me, “Son of man, set in your heart, see with your eyes, and hear with your ears everything I speak with you concerning all the commands of the Lord’s house and all its ordinances. Set your heart on the house’s entrance, according to all its exits in all the holy places.

target_units.text: The man said to me, ‘Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes, hear with your ears and set in your heart everything I show you, for you have entered here so that it might be shown to you. You will show Israel’s house everything you see.’

triples.relationship: close declaration of enough followed by a demand to end wrongdoing
triples.rationale: God says Israel's lawless deeds must be enough. The following ruler instructions likewise say Enough to Israel's rulers and command removal of injustice and oppression. The shared declaration and demand are retained with the different groups addressed.
triples.source_text: You will say to the provoking house, to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Let all your lawless deeds be enough for you, house of Israel—

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord God: Enough, rulers of Israel! Remove injustice and suffering, and practice judgment and righteousness. Take oppression away from My people, says the Lord God.

triples.relationship: related distinction between circumcision of flesh and heart
triples.rationale: Ezekiel describes admitted foreigners as uncircumcised in both heart and flesh. Jeremiah's judgment declaration likewise distinguishes uncircumcision in flesh and heart, assigning them to nations and Israel respectively. The two dimensions connect them; the groups are not made identical.
triples.source_text: —your bringing in foreign sons, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My holy places. They profaned them while you offered bread, fat, and blood, and you transgressed My covenant in all your lawless deeds.

target_units.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will visit all who have been circumcised in their foreskins:

Egypt and Judea and Edom and the sons of Ammon and the sons of Moab and everyone who clips the hair around his face, those dwelling in the wilderness; because all the nations are uncircumcised in flesh, and all Israel’s house are uncircumcised in their hearts.

triples.relationship: related charge of sanctuary profanation through bringing in foreigners
triples.rationale: Ezekiel condemns the admission of foreign sons uncircumcised in heart and flesh into the holy places as profanation. In Acts, Paul's accusers charge him with defiling the holy place by bringing Greeks into it, but the narrator explains this as their supposition about Trophimus. The parallel is the form of the charge, not a claim that Paul actually committed it.
triples.source_text: —your bringing in foreign sons, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My holy places. They profaned them while you offered bread, fat, and blood, and you transgressed My covenant in all your lawless deeds.

target_units.text: crying, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against the people, the law, and this place. Moreover, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”
For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

triples.relationship: related arrangement for keeping sacred duties
triples.rationale: The source positively says that the addressees arranged the keeping of duties in the holy places. Chronicles likewise assigns keeping the Tent's and Aaron's sons' charges for ministry in the Lord's house. The source is not reversed into an accusation that no duties were arranged.
triples.source_text: You arranged for the keeping of duties in My holy places.

target_units.text: They shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony and the charges of Aaron’s sons their brethren, to minister in the Lord’s house.

triples.relationship: related exclusion of the uncircumcised from a holy place
triples.rationale: Ezekiel forbids an uncircumcised foreign son to enter the holy places, expressly naming heart and flesh. Isaiah says no uncircumcised and unclean person will again pass through holy Jerusalem. The exclusion and holiness connect them while the sanctuary, city and stated qualifications remain distinct.
triples.source_text: Therefore thus says the Lord God: No foreign son uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh will enter My holy places, among all the foreign sons who are in the midst of the house of Israel,

target_units.text: Awake, awake, Zion! Clothe yourself with your strength, Zion, and put on your glory, Jerusalem, holy city. No uncircumcised and unclean person will pass through you again.

triples.relationship: related consequences for Levitical ministry that has strayed
triples.rationale: The Levites sprang away when Israel strayed and will receive their injustice. Malachi likewise condemns turning aside from the way and corrupting Levi's covenant, followed by disgrace. The source's reflections are preserved without translating that word into a different object of devotion.
triples.source_text: except the Levites, who sprang away from Me when Israel strayed from Me after their reflections; they will receive their injustice—

target_units.text: But you have turned aside from the way and weakened many through the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the Lord Almighty.
“And I have made you despised and neglected among all the nations, because you did not guard My ways but showed partiality in the law.”

triples.relationship: related Levitical service distinguished from priestly approach
triples.rationale: Ezekiel assigns these Levites gatekeeping, house ministry and slaughtering for the people. Numbers likewise appoints Levites to minister and keep the Tent's charges while restricting their approach to holy vessels and altar. The shared supporting service does not make Numbers enumerate this source's slaughtering tasks.
triples.source_text: —and will serve in My holy places as gatekeepers at the house’s gates and as ministers to the house. They will slaughter the burnt offerings and sacrifices for the people, and stand before the people to serve them.

target_units.text: And bring your brethren, the tribe of Levi, your father’s clan, near unto you; and let them join you and minister unto you; and you and your sons with you shall be before the Tent of Testimony.
And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.
And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.

triples.relationship: related harm and judgment associated with failed Levitical ministry
triples.rationale: Ezekiel says their ministry before idols became a punishment of injustice for Israel, and God raised His hand against them. Malachi says the priests weakened many through the law and corrupted Levi's covenant; God says He made them despised and neglected. The harmful ministry and consequence connect them without adding an explicit oath to the source's raised hand.
triples.source_text: Because they ministered to them before their idols, and it became a punishment of injustice for the house of Israel, I raised My hand against them, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: But you have turned aside from the way and weakened many through the law; you have corrupted the covenant of Levi,” says the Lord Almighty.
“And I have made you despised and neglected among all the nations, because you did not guard My ways but showed partiality in the law.”

triples.relationship: related exclusion from priestly altar service
triples.rationale: Ezekiel denies the straying ministers priestly approach and access to the most holy things. Kings likewise says the high-place priests did not go up to the Lord's altar in Jerusalem, although they ate unleavened bread among their brothers. The restriction is shared without identifying the two groups as the same people.
triples.source_text: They will not draw near to Me to serve Me as priests, nor approach the holy things of the sons of Israel, nor My most holy things. They will receive their dishonor in the straying by which they strayed.

target_units.text: He brought up all the priests from Judah’s cities and defiled the high places where the priests burned incense, from Gabaa to Beersheba. He pulled down the house of the gates beside the doorway of the gate of Joshua, the city’s ruler, on a man’s left at the city gate.
Nevertheless, the priests of the high places did not go up to the Lord’s altar in Jerusalem; they only ate unleavened bread among their brothers.

triples.relationship: close assignment of Levitical custodial service with restricted approach
triples.rationale: The ministers remain assigned to keep the house's duties and carry out its work, following the denial of priestly access. Numbers likewise assigns Levites the Tent's charges but excludes approach to the holy vessels and altar. The common distinction of duties does not make the target's appointment a punishment for this source's offense.
triples.source_text: They will assign them to keep the duties of the house, for all its works and everything they may do.

target_units.text: And they shall keep your charges and the charges of the Tent; only they shall not approach the holy vessels and the altar, that neither they nor you may die.
And they shall join you, and shall keep the charges of the Tent of Testimony according to all the ministries of the Tent; and the outsider shall not approach you.

triples.relationship: close Zadokite priests who draw near to minister
triples.rationale: The sons of Zadok approach and minister because they kept the holy places' duties during Israel's straying. The earlier chamber description likewise identifies Zadok's sons as those who draw near to the Lord to minister. The source adds the explanation of their fidelity.
triples.source_text: The Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept the duties of My holy places when the house of Israel strayed from Me, will approach Me to minister to Me. They will stand before Me to offer sacrifice, fat, and blood to Me, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: and the recessed chamber facing north is for the priests who keep the altar’s charge. They are Zadok’s sons, who draw near to the Lord from Levi to minister to Him.’

triples.relationship: close priestly approach to the Lord's table
triples.rationale: The faithful priests approach God's table to minister. The earlier furnishing is expressly identified as the table before the Lord. The common table designation connects service and furnishing without making the source repeat the earlier altar's measurements.
triples.source_text: They will enter My holy places and approach My table to minister to Me, and they will keep My duties.

target_units.text: of a wooden altar, three cubits high, two cubits long, and two cubits broad. It had horns, and its base and its walls were wood. He said to me, “This is the table before the Lord.”

triples.relationship: close linen garments for priestly entry into holy service
triples.rationale: Ezekiel requires linen robes for entering the inner court and forbids wool during that service. Leviticus likewise prescribes holy linen clothing for Aaron's entrance, including tunic, undergarments, belt and turban. The source's express wool prohibition is an additional instruction, not quoted from Leviticus.
triples.source_text: When they enter the gates of the inner court, they will put on linen robes. They will not wear woolen things when they minister from the gate of the inner court.

target_units.text: And he shall put on a consecrated linen tunic, with linen undergarments against his skin, gird himself with a linen belt, and put on a linen turban. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his whole body in water and put them on.

triples.relationship: close linen headwear and undergarments for priestly service
triples.rationale: The priests wear linen turbans and linen trousers. Aaron's prescribed holy garments likewise include a linen turban and linen undergarments. The source's additional command not to bind clothing tightly is not recast as a different statement about sweat.
triples.source_text: They will have linen turbans on their heads and linen trousers on their hips, and they will not bind their clothing tightly.

target_units.text: And he shall put on a consecrated linen tunic, with linen undergarments against his skin, gird himself with a linen belt, and put on a linen turban. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his whole body in water and put them on.

triples.relationship: close changing ministry garments before going among the people
triples.rationale: The priests leave ministry robes in the holy chambers and put on other robes before going to the people. The earlier chamber instruction likewise requires other garments when they come into contact with the people. The source explicitly says they must not sanctify the people with their robes.
triples.source_text: When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they will take off the robes in which they minister, place them in the recessed chambers of the holy places, and put on other robes. They will certainly not sanctify the people with their robes.

target_units.text: No one will enter there except the priests. They will not go out from the holy place into the outer court, so that those who bring offerings may always be holy and may not touch the garments in which they minister, for they are holy. They will put on other garments whenever they come into contact with the people.”

triples.relationship: related restrictions on priestly shaving
triples.rationale: Ezekiel prohibits shaving the head or stripping away hair and positively requires covering the head. Leviticus likewise forbids a bald patch for a dead person, adding beard-shaving and bodily-cutting restrictions. The related hair rules are bounded by their different particulars; covering is not changed to trimming.
triples.source_text: They will not shave their heads or strip away their hair; they will certainly cover their heads.

target_units.text: And you shall not shave a bald patch on your head for a dead person. They shall not shave the face of their beard or cut incisions in their flesh.

triples.relationship: close prohibition of wine when entering holy service
triples.rationale: Ezekiel forbids priests to drink wine when entering the inner court. Leviticus similarly prohibits wine and strong drink for Aaron and his sons when entering the Tent or approaching the altar. The priestly abstinence and entrance setting are shared without equating the named spaces.
triples.source_text: No priest will drink wine when they enter the inner court.

target_units.text: You shall drink no wine or strong drink, you and your sons with you, when you enter the Tent of Testimony, or when you approach the altar, so that you do not die: an everlasting statute throughout your generations,

triples.relationship: related priestly marriage rules with a differing widow allowance
triples.rationale: Ezekiel requires a virgin of Israel and excludes divorced women, but permits a priest's widow. The Levitical high-priest instruction requires a virgin and excludes widows as well as expelled women. The shared restrictions and explicit difference are preserved with the target's high-priest scope.
triples.source_text: They will not take a widow or a woman who has been sent away as a wife, but a virgin of Israel’s offspring; if she is a priest’s widow, they may take her.

target_units.text: He shall take a virgin wife from his own kin.
A widow, an expelled woman, a profaned woman, or a prostitute—these he shall not take. He shall take as his wife only a virgin from his own kin.

triples.relationship: close priestly teaching of holy and clean distinctions
triples.rationale: Ezekiel requires teaching the difference between holy and profane and between unclean and clean. Leviticus joins those same distinctions with instruction of Israel in God's statutes. The double distinction and teaching responsibility make the connection particular.
triples.source_text: They will teach My people the difference between holy and profane, and make known to them the difference between unclean and clean.

target_units.text: to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.

triples.relationship: close priestly judgment in blood cases
triples.rationale: Ezekiel assigns the priests decision-making in blood cases according to God's judgments. Deuteronomy likewise sends difficult blood and other disputes to Levitical priests and the judge, requiring observance of their judgment. The source's festival and Sabbath duties remain additional instructions.
triples.source_text: In a case involving blood they will stand to decide. They will uphold My judgments and judge My decisions; they will keep My ordinances and My commands at all My festivals, and sanctify My Sabbaths.

target_units.text: And if a matter in judgment is too hard for you, between blood and blood, and between judgment and judgment, and between injury and injury, and between dispute and dispute, matters of judgment within your cities, you shall arise and go up unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there.
And you shall come unto the Levitical priests, and unto the judge who shall be in those days; and they shall inquire, and declare unto you the judgment.

And you shall do according to the matter which they declare unto you from the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there; and you shall take diligent heed to do according to all that is laid down for you as law.
You shall do according to the law and according to the judgment which they tell you; you shall not turn aside from the word which they declare unto you, to the right hand or to the left.

triples.relationship: close priestly corpse-defilement rule and listed family exceptions
triples.rationale: The source bars corpse defilement but allows it for father, mother, children, brother and a sister not belonging to a husband. Leviticus gives the same immediate-family exceptions and specifies the unmarried virgin sister. The listed relationships, rather than a general purity theme, supply the close connection.
triples.source_text: They will not approach a human corpse so as to be defiled, except that a priest may be defiled for his father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or sister who has not belonged to a husband.

target_units.text: And the Lord said unto Moses, saying: Speak unto the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say unto them: They shall not be defiled for dead persons among their nation,
except for their nearest household kin: father, mother, sons, daughters, and brother;
and for a virgin sister near to him who has not been given to a man—for these he may defile himself.

triples.relationship: related corpse-purification periods with different timing
triples.rationale: Following the corpse rule, the source counts seven days after the priest is cleansed. Numbers assigns seven days of uncleanness after touching a corpse and purification on the third and seventh days. The corpse context and seven-day periods connect them, while before and after cleansing are not harmonized.
triples.source_text: After he has been cleansed, one will count seven days for him.

target_units.text: Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

triples.relationship: related atonement offering for entry into holy service
triples.rationale: Ezekiel requires an atonement offering on entering the inner court to minister, following the purification instructions. Leviticus likewise prescribes a calf for sin when Aaron enters the holy place and atonement for himself and his house. The entry-and-offering relationship is shared without equating the occasions or priestly scopes.
triples.source_text: On whatever day they enter the inner court to minister in the holy place, they will bring an atonement offering, says the Lord God.

target_units.text: In this way Aaron shall enter the holy place: with a calf from the cattle for sin and a ram for a whole burnt offering.

And he shall put on a consecrated linen tunic, with linen undergarments against his skin, gird himself with a linen belt, and put on a linen turban. These are holy garments. He shall bathe his whole body in water and put them on.
And from the congregation of the sons of Israel he shall take two male young goats from the goats for sin and one ram for a whole burnt offering.
And Aaron shall present the calf for his sin offering and make atonement for himself and his house.

triples.relationship: close God as the priests' inheritance instead of land
triples.rationale: God declares Himself the priests' inheritance and possession, so they receive no possession among Israel. The Lord likewise tells Aaron that he receives no land portion because God is his portion and inheritance. The distinctive replacement of landed inheritance by God Himself is explicit in both.
triples.source_text: This will be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. No possession will be given them among the sons of Israel, because I am their possession.

target_units.text: And the Lord spoke unto Aaron: You shall not inherit in their land, neither shall you have a portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.

triples.relationship: close priestly portions from holy offerings and devoted things
triples.rationale: Ezekiel assigns sacrificial, sin and ignorance offerings to the priests, together with everything set apart in Israel. Numbers likewise assigns consecrated sin and guilt offerings to Aaron and his sons, and also assigns everything devoted to the priestly recipient. The shared food and devoted-property provisions are preserved with each passage's own offering terms.
triples.source_text: They will eat the sacrifices, the offerings for sin, and the offerings for ignorance. Everything set apart in Israel will belong to them.

target_units.text: And this shall be yours from the consecrated holy offerings: from all their gifts, and from all their sacrifices, and from every guilt offering of theirs, and from all their sin offerings which they render unto Me; from all the holy things it shall be yours and your sons’.
You shall eat them in the most holy place; every male shall eat them, you and your sons; they shall be holy unto you.

And this shall be yours, the firstfruits of their gifts: from all the presentations of the sons of Israel, I have given them unto you, and unto your sons and unto your daughters with you, an everlasting ordinance. Everyone clean in your house shall eat them.
Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

triples.relationship: close priestly entitlement to first produce and firstborn gifts
triples.rationale: Ezekiel assigns firstfruits, firstborn and contributions to priests and connects first produce with blessing upon households. Numbers likewise grants firstfruits, first produce and what opens the womb, there adding redemption requirements. The entitlement is shared without importing the target's redemption details or the source's household-blessing clause into the other passage.
triples.source_text: The firstfruits of everything, the firstborn of everything, and all the contributions from all your firstfruits will belong to the priests. You will give your first produce to the priest, to place your blessings upon your houses.

target_units.text: Every firstfruit of oil, and every firstfruit of wine and grain, their firstfruits which they give unto the Lord, I have given them unto you.
All the first produce in their land, which they bring unto the Lord, shall be yours; everyone clean in your house shall eat it.
Everything devoted among the sons of Israel shall be yours.

And everything that opens the womb of all flesh, which they present unto the Lord, from man unto livestock, shall be yours; but the firstborn of men shall surely be redeemed, and you shall redeem the firstborn of unclean livestock.

triples.relationship: close prohibition of carrion and animals torn by beasts for priests
triples.rationale: Ezekiel forbids priests to eat creatures that died of themselves or were taken by a beast, expressly including birds and livestock. Leviticus likewise prohibits an animal found dead or torn by beasts as defiling food. The source's specified creature categories remain additional detail.
triples.source_text: The priests will not eat anything that has died of itself or has been taken by a beast, whether from the birds or from the livestock.”

target_units.text: He shall not eat an animal found dead or torn by beasts, becoming unclean through them. I am the Lord.

deferred_source_units.source_text: and the chamber, one reed long and one reed wide; the porch between the chambers was six cubits. The second chamber was one reed wide and one reed long, and the porch five cubits,
deferred_source_units.reason: The two reed-square chambers and differing intervening porch dimensions were read. No independent particular counterpart to that combination was retained; equal dimensions alone were not multiplied into extra connections.

deferred_source_units.source_text: and the third chamber was one reed wide and one reed long,
deferred_source_units.reason: The third reed-square chamber continues the chamber enumeration. A separate reference based only on repeating the adjacent chamber size was not retained.
